A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OpenHands platform and contain readable main text and Appendices A-K. Tables, figures, runtime documentation, and prompts can be matched across the changed pagination.

before.justification: Tables 3-7 report original evaluations of OpenHands agents, including task success rates, execution costs, and additional GPQA subset results in Appendix G.

after.justification: V3 retains original OpenHands evaluations across software engineering, web browsing, and assistance tasks, including the appendix GPQA results.

M1.justification: The event-stream architecture, Docker runtime, AgentSkills, delegation mechanism, and agent implementations remain unchanged. The appendix prompts, tool interfaces, and runtime procedures also match; no procedural modification is documented.

E1.justification: Table 4 removes the 50-instance BioCoder Java evaluation while retaining the 157-instance Python evaluation, narrowing reported language coverage within one benchmark. All 15 benchmark families remain. Java is still mentioned in the dataset description, but its results are not relocated.

E2.justification: Table 5 removes the Llama3-chat-8b and Llama3-chat-70b WebArena Agent comparators. Table 6 removes the human comparator for Entity Deduction Arena. Other retained comparator sets are unchanged; the newly discussed frameworks are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported WebArena model configurations narrow: Table 5 omits BrowsingAgent v1.0 with gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, alongside the removed Llama3 comparator configurations. Splits, metrics, and testing procedures for retained results remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 loses brief qualitative diagnostics about potential hallucination and syntax-error reductions on ML-Bench and ToolQA's stronger CSV/database performance versus math/calculator weaknesses. No controlled ablation or robustness study is added, and the supplementary GPQA comparisons remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and average costs without run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Removed entries include BioCoder Java scores of 44.0% for OpenHands and 4.1%/6.4% for prompting; WebArena scores of 3.3%/7.0% for the Llama3 baselines and 5.2% for OpenHands with GPT-3.5; and the EDA human score of 21.0%. Retained numerical results, including Appendix G, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The state, action, and observation abstractions remain unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theoretical results, proofs, or mathematical derivations that differ between versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same generalist-platform contribution, sandboxed interaction, multi-agent support, and 15-benchmark evaluation claim. The central claim of competitive generality across task categories is unchanged.

C2.justification: Most benchmark-specific interpretation in Section 4 is removed, including generalist-versus-specialist browsing trade-offs, GAIA's multimodal dependence, attribution of GPQA gains to tools, and AgentBench's minimum-model-capability argument. This substantially reduces the interpretation of empirical findings, although Appendix A's explicit limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 removes the front-page Benchmark access link and Section 4.3's description of WebArena's handwritten success checks. Code access and the detailed runtime, integration-test, tool, and prompt documentation in the appendices remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds discussion of LangChain/LangGraph, CrewAI, BrowserGym, DSPy, and AutoGen, including differences in runtime and orchestration capabilities. CrewAI and DSPy references are added; the Qwen technical-report reference is removed.

P1.justification: Section 4 is shortened by deleting many per-benchmark Results passages, Appendix C gains one paragraph, and the header changes to ICLR 2025 publication status. The section sequence and most architectural, introductory, and concluding prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 4-6 become shorter through row and block removals, and retained displays reflow across pages. Figure 5 is reduced to share a page with text. All five figures and seven tables remain, with unchanged diagram content and basic visual design.

improvement.justification: Expanded related-work coverage and shorter prose provide modest benefits, but v3 removes the complete BioCoder Java comparison and several comparator/model results without replacement. Java remains in the benchmark description, making evaluated coverage less clear. These losses reduce empirical completeness and interpretability, while the unchanged platform contribution and most retained evidence limit the overall deterioration.
